classification.difficultyReason: Part a is a standard logistic solve. Part b needs C found from two data points by eliminating A, the same demand as p80-q1 with k given.

content.prompt: Each population below follows a logistic model, with $t$ in years.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
The number of Murray cod $P$ in a dam satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.0003P(1200-P)$, where $t$ is the time since the dam was stocked with 200 cod.

Use $\dfrac{1}{P(1200-P)}=\dfrac{1}{1200}\left(\dfrac1P+\dfrac1{1200-P}\right)$ to find $P$ in terms of $t$, and hence the limiting population.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{P(1200-P)}\,dP&=0.0003\,dt\\\frac{1}{1200}\int\left(\frac1P+\frac1{1200-P}\right)dP&=\int0.0003\,dt\\\ln P-\ln(1200-P)&=0.36t+k\\\frac{P}{1200-P}&=Ae^{0.36t}\end{align*}$$
When $t=0$, $P=200$, so $A=\dfrac{200}{1000}=\dfrac15$.
$$\begin{align*}5P&=(1200-P)e^{0.36t}\\P&=\frac{1200}{1+5e^{-0.36t}}\end{align*}$$
As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-0.36t}\to0$, so $P\to1200$.
The limiting population is $1200$ cod.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
The number of kangaroos $P$ on a sanctuary satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.1P\left(1-\dfrac PC\right)$, where $t$ is the time since 2015 and $C$ is a constant. There were 1500 kangaroos in 2015 and 3200 in 2025.

Use $\dfrac{1}{P(C-P)}=\dfrac1C\left(\dfrac1P+\dfrac1{C-P}\right)$ to find the limiting population, to the nearest hundred.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dP}{dt}&=\frac{0.1P(C-P)}{C}\\\frac{1}{P(C-P)}\,dP&=\frac{0.1}{C}\,dt\\\int\left(\frac1P+\frac1{C-P}\right)dP&=\int0.1\,dt\\\ln P-\ln(C-P)&=0.1t+k\\\frac{P}{C-P}&=Ae^{0.1t}\end{align*}$$
The two data points give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{1500}{C-1500}&=A\\\frac{3200}{C-3200}&=Ae.\end{align*}$$
Dividing eliminates $A$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3200(C-1500)}{1500(C-3200)}&=e\\32(C-1500)&=15e(C-3200)\\(15e-32)C&=48\,000(e-1)\\C&=\frac{48\,000(e-1)}{15e-32}\end{align*}$$
As $t\to\infty$, $P\to C$.
The limiting population is $9400$ kangaroos, to the nearest hundred.
